title: Training helps early; the ask-versus-got gap remains
words: Training helps early. The remaining gap persists. More epochs initially bring achieved win rates closer to requests. The later checkpoints show no clear further reduction in error. Most observed improvement is early 66.2% lower error Epoch 1 → epoch 34, same sampling seed. Further gain uncertain Epochs 34–80 stay near 0.006. 0.000 0.005 0.010 0.015 0.020 0.025 0.030 1 21 34 55 80 Ask-versus-got error Training epoch Later gain uncertain Target < 0.001: none reaches it 0.01750 Epoch 34: 0.00591 0.00600 Error is the mean squared gap between each request and its mean achieved win rate, over requests 1/24 to 17/24. Lower is better. Dots are observed checkpoints; lines guide the eye. Thin bars are 95% intervals from whole-team and shared-opponent bootstraps. They exclude variation between training runs. Higher requests still miss the diagonal Ask 70.8% Epoch 34 gets 51.8% Epoch 80 gets 52.8% This request is 17/24, inside the scored range. Training longer leaves a large observed gap here; these two means do not establish a better checkpoint. Counts are unique across all 1,472 generated teams. Full 66 points is the share of Pokémon spending all available Stat Points. Team spread is the average within-request standard deviation of team win rates. New line-up reference: 54,766 distinct six-species line-ups from 170,785 labelled non-validation rows, fixed before rule-table filtering. Five rows were excluded from actual training. Novelty here is relative to that larger reference. Uncertainty: 95% percentile bootstrap; whole teams within each ask and shared opponent columns across epochs; original opponent weights retained One training run, seed 0; sampling seed 1 at every checkpoint; 64 teams at each of 23 requests. Each team plays the 49 distinct top-50 opponents with behaviour-cloning on both sides and shuffled slots. The duplicated meta entry has score weight 2, giving total weight 50. The labelled-only model generates all 84 fields with label noise ±1/48. Stat Alignment is repaired to match the moves. These samples use no search or elite-selection rule. Three-sampling-seed summaries stay separate: epoch 21, error 0.0066; epoch 80, error 0.0053. They are not substituted into the one-seed curve. This is exploratory evidence from one training run. Epoch 34 is the lowest observed one-seed error, not a proven optimum. Epoch 80 is the training cap and lowest validation-loss checkpoint. No measured checkpoint reaches the near-line threshold of 0.001. All 14,720 seed-1 teams have 49/49 opponent coverage and exactly 49 battles. Weighted matrix scores reproduce every saved score. The original checkpoint files matched all ten recorded hashes. Epoch-80 preflight passed, including its 20-team round trip. The battle database records showdown:unknown for the simulator revision. The figure storyboard was written retrospectively from the recorded results. It orders the explanation as early improvement, remaining mismatch, then a single-view teaser. It is not a pre-registration.
